q-asien-altertum-32#explanation: Silk, lacquer and paper went west, while horses, glass, gems and silver came east in return. Religions such as Buddhism travelled with the goods.
q-asien-altertum-33#question: Which religion did the Sasanians make the state religion of Persia?
q-asien-altertum-33#explanation: Zarathustra's teaching of the struggle between good and evil influenced Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Jews, Christians and Manichaeans also lived in the Sasanian Empire.
q-asien-altertum-34#question: Which city was the capital of the Tang dynasty and, with around a million inhabitants, the largest city in the world?
q-asien-altertum-34#explanation: Chang'an was laid out on a grid, and Persians, Sogdians, Indians and Arabs traded in its markets. Kaifeng and Hangzhou only became cities of a million under the Song.
q-asien-altertum-35#question: Which novel turned the monk Xuanzang's journey to India into a popular legend?
q-asien-altertum-35#explanation: In the 16th-century novel the Monkey King accompanies the monk on his pilgrimage. The real Xuanzang brought hundreds of Buddhist scriptures back to Chang'an in 645.
q-asien-altertum-36#question: How did the Heian period in Japan end in 1185?
q-asien-altertum-36#choices.0: With the conquest of Japan by China
q-asien-altertum-36#choices.2: With the establishment of the first shogunate
q-asien-altertum-36#choices.3: With the move of the court to Nara
q-asien-altertum-36#explanation: After the war between the warrior clans of Minamoto and Taira, power passed from the court nobility to the warriors. The emperor remained but no longer ruled himself.
q-asien-altertum-37#question: What were the ingredients of the gunpowder whose recipe was recorded in Song China in 1044?
q-asien-altertum-37#explanation: The military manual Wujing Zongyao described mixtures for fire arrows and bombs. Fire lances and explosive bombs followed in the 12th century.
q-asien-altertum-38#question: What was the purpose of China's Grand Canal?
q-asien-altertum-38#choices.0: It linked northern and southern China and secured the rice supply of the capitals
q-asien-altertum-38#choices.1: It protected the frontier against the nomads
q-asien-altertum-38#choices.2: It carried water into the Gobi Desert
q-asien-altertum-38#choices.3: It connected China with the Indian Ocean
q-asien-altertum-38#explanation: The canal carried rice from the fertile south to the north, where the capitals lay. It is still the longest artificial waterway in the world.
q-asien-altertum-39#choices.1: Murasaki Shikibu writes The Tale of Genji
q-asien-altertum-39#explanation: The Tang were founded in 618, Wu Zetian took the throne in 690, the Diamond Sutra was printed in 868 and The Tale of Genji was completed around 1008. It was written at the Japanese imperial court in the Heian period.
q-asien-altertum-40#question: Where did the Buddha give his first sermon?
q-asien-altertum-40#choices.0: Under the fig tree at Bodhgaya
q-asien-altertum-40#choices.3: In the deer park at Sarnath
q-asien-altertum-40#explanation: Siddhartha attained enlightenment at Bodhgaya and began teaching at Sarnath. He then spent about four decades as a wandering teacher in northern India.
q-asien-altertum-41#question: What does the Daoist term wuwei mean?
q-asien-altertum-41#explanation: The Daodejing recommends restraint and non-interference even to the ruler. In this Daoism stood in contrast to Confucius' rules and ceremonies.
q-asien-altertum-42#question: Which work from the time of Ashoka is today the state emblem of India?
q-asien-altertum-42#choices.2: The lion capital of the pillar at Sarnath
q-asien-altertum-42#explanation: Ashoka had pillars erected bearing edicts on tolerance and non-violence. The Ajanta paintings date from the Gupta period and the Thanjavur temple from the Cholas.
q-asien-altertum-43#question: Which envoy did Emperor Wu of Han send west to seek allies against the Xiongnu?
q-asien-altertum-43#explanation: Zhang Qian's reports on Central Asia led to regular caravans and thus to the Silk Road. Bi Sheng later invented movable type, and Li Bai was a poet of the Tang era.
q-asien-altertum-44#question: Since when has the name Silk Road existed?
q-asien-altertum-44#explanation: The term was only coined by European scholars in the 19th century. The traders themselves knew no single network by this name, only individual caravan and sea routes.
q-asien-altertum-45#question: What is the art of Gandhara in the Kushan Empire especially known for?
q-asien-altertum-45#choices.1: Early statues of the Buddha in human form in a Greek-influenced style
q-asien-altertum-45#choices.3: The largest temple pyramids in Asia
q-asien-altertum-45#explanation: The sculptors of Gandhara combined Greek and Indian stylistic elements. From there monks and texts of Mahayana Buddhism travelled to Central Asia and China.
q-asien-altertum-46#question: Which city on the Tigris was the capital of the Sasanians?
q-asien-altertum-46#explanation: Ardashir I made Ctesiphon his capital after his victory over the Parthians in 224. Persepolis and Pasargadae were residences of the earlier Achaemenids.
q-asien-altertum-47#question: Which drama by the Gupta poet Kalidasa also delighted Goethe after it was translated?
q-asien-altertum-47#explanation: Shakuntala tells of a king's love for a hermit's daughter, whom he forgets because of a curse. The first German translation in 1791 sparked European enthusiasm for Indian poetry.
q-asien-altertum-48#question: Which event from 755 onwards began the Tang dynasty's loss of power?
q-asien-altertum-48#choices.2: The founding of the Sasanian Empire
q-asien-altertum-48#choices.3: The building of the Great Wall
q-asien-altertum-48#explanation: After the uprising of the general An Lushan the court gradually lost control of the provinces. The dynasty nevertheless lasted until 907.
q-asien-altertum-49#question: Which work did Sei Shonagon, Murasaki Shikibu's rival at the Japanese court, write?
q-asien-altertum-49#explanation: The Pillow Book is a collection of observations, anecdotes and lists from court life in the Heian period. Like Murasaki, she wrote in Japanese syllabic script.
q-asien-altertum-50#question: What are the underground channels used in Persia to irrigate fields called?
q-asien-altertum-50#explanation: Qanats carry groundwater to the fields through long, gently sloping tunnels without it evaporating in the heat. The technique is still in use today.
q-asien-altertum-51#question: Against which kingdom on Sumatra did the Chola king Rajendra I send a fleet in 1025?
q-asien-altertum-51#explanation: With this attack the Cholas sought to control the sea routes to China. Rajendra's father Rajaraja I had already subjugated Sri Lanka and built the temple at Thanjavur.
q-asien-altertum-52#question: Which sage did the emperors of the Tang dynasty regard as their ancestor?
q-asien-altertum-52#explanation: The Tang emperors bore the family name Li, which tradition also gave to Laozi. In religious Daoism Laozi was worshipped as a deity.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-01: Which event triggered the First World War in the summer of 1914?
The murder of the Austrian heir to the throne, Franz Ferdinand, on June 28, 1914 in Sarajevo led through the July Crisis into war.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-02: Who led the Bolsheviks to power in the October Revolution of 1917?
Lenin returned from exile in April 1917 and in November led the overthrow in Petrograd.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-03: On which day did the Armistice of Compiègne come into force?
The armistice came into force at 11 o'clock on November 11, 1918 and ended the fighting on the Western Front.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-04: Which great power never joined the League of Nations, although its president had proposed it?
The American Senate rejected membership, although Woodrow Wilson had outlined the League of Nations in his Fourteen Points.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-05: Which reform was NOT part of Atatürk's transformation of Turkey?
Atatürk abolished the caliphate in 1924; he carried through the other reforms in the 1920s and 1930s.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-06: What was Gandhi's Salt March of 1930 directed against?
Against the import of British cloth
Against the British salt monopoly and the salt tax
Gandhi marched 385 kilometers to the sea and there demonstratively extracted salt, which was forbidden under British law.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-07: Through which achievement did Mustafa Kemal become known in 1915?
The defense of Gallipoli against the Allies
As a colonel, Mustafa Kemal and his troops held the heights of the Gallipoli peninsula; the Allies had to withdraw in January 1916.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-08: Which new currency ended the hyperinflation in Germany in November 1923?
The Rentenmark, introduced on November 15, 1923, stabilized the currency; the Reichsmark replaced it in 1924.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-09: Who was the first woman to give a speech in a German parliament, on February 19, 1919?
The Social Democrat Marie Juchacz spoke in the Weimar National Assembly and in the same year founded the Arbeiterwohlfahrt welfare organization.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-10: Which school of art, craft and design did Walter Gropius found in Weimar in 1919?
The Bauhaus moved to Dessau in 1925 and was closed by the National Socialists in 1933; its influence on architecture and design continues to this day.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-11: What did the stab-in-the-back myth claim after the First World War?
That the Allies had broken the armistice
That the emperor had betrayed the army
That the army, undefeated in the field, had been betrayed by the home front and the politicians
That the reparations had been invented by France
Hindenburg and Ludendorff spread the myth in order to conceal their own responsibility for the defeat; it served the opponents of the republic as a propaganda weapon.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-12: What did Germany's Schlieffen Plan envisage at the start of the First World War?
A defensive war in the west and a quick attack on Russia
A naval blockade of Britain as the first step of the war
A joint advance with Italy against France across the Alps
A quick victory over France by advancing through Belgium, then turning against Russia
The plan was meant to avoid a two-front war but failed on the Marne. The invasion of neutral Belgium also brought Britain into the war.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-13: On which river was the German advance on Paris halted in September 1914?
After the Battle of the Marne both sides dug in; the Western Front froze into trench warfare for almost four years.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-14: Which countries did the ANZAC troops who landed at Gallipoli in 1915 come from?
ANZAC stands for Australian and New Zealand Army Corps. The anniversary of the landing, 25 April, is still a national day of remembrance in both countries.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-15: Against which population group was the genocide directed that the Young Turk government committed in the Ottoman Empire from 1915?
Hundreds of thousands to well over a million Armenians died in deportations into the Syrian desert and in massacres. The German Bundestag recognised the crimes as genocide in 2016.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-16: Around which French fortress town did a ten-month battle of attrition rage in 1916?
The Battle of Verdun caused more than 700,000 dead and wounded without significantly moving the front. It became a symbol of senseless mass death in trench warfare.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-17: Where did the German army first use chlorine gas on a large scale in April 1915?
The gas attack at Ypres on 22 April 1915 was prepared with the help of the chemist Fritz Haber. Soon all warring parties were using poison gas.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-18: Which theme shapes the work of the artist Käthe Kollwitz?
Glamorous big-city scenes of the Golden Twenties
Abstract geometric forms in the Bauhaus style
The suffering of mothers, the poor and victims of war
Kollwitz lost her son Peter in the war in 1914. Her sculptures of the "Grieving Parents" stand in the Vladslo war cemetery in Belgium.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-19: What did Britain promise in the Balfour Declaration of 1917?
Support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine
Independence for India after the war
The return of Alsace-Lorraine to France
An independent Arab kingdom from Damascus to Baghdad
The declaration by Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour contradicted promises made to the Arabs and laid one of the foundations of the Middle East conflict.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-20: What did Germany offer Mexico in the 1917 Zimmermann Telegram in return for an alliance against the USA?
The recovery of Texas, New Mexico and Arizona
British codebreakers intercepted the telegram; its publication in March 1917, together with submarine warfare, contributed to the US entry into the war in April.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-21: Which of these happened first in Russia?
The abdication of Tsar Nicholas II
The founding of the Soviet Union
The tsar abdicated after the February Revolution in March 1917; then came the October Revolution of 1917, the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in 1918 and the founding of the Soviet Union at the end of 1922.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-22: With which peace treaty did Soviet Russia leave the First World War in 1918?
Russia lost Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine. After Germany's defeat in November 1918 the treaty was annulled.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-23: In which city did the sailors' mutiny that sparked the November Revolution begin in early November 1918?

Sailors had previously refused to put to sea for a hopeless final battle against the British fleet; in Kiel they demanded the release of their arrested comrades. Within days, workers' and soldiers' councils formed throughout the Reich.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-24: Who proclaimed the German Republic from the Reichstag building in Berlin on 9 November 1918?
The Social Democrat Scheidemann pre-empted Karl Liebknecht, who a few hours later proclaimed a "free socialist republic" from the Berlin Palace.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-25: Why was the influenza pandemic of 1918 called the "Spanish flu"?
Because it had demonstrably broken out in Madrid
Because Spanish troops brought it to the Western Front
Because the press in neutral Spain, free of wartime censorship, reported on it openly
Because a Spanish doctor discovered its pathogen
In the warring countries censorship suppressed reports of the epidemic, so it first became known from Spain. The pandemic killed more people worldwide than the First World War.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-26: In which election were women in Germany first allowed to vote and stand for office nationwide?
The election to the National Assembly in 1919
Women's suffrage was introduced in November 1918 by the Council of People's Deputies. On 19 January 1919, 37 women were elected to the National Assembly.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-27: Which territory did Germany have to return to France under the Treaty of Versailles?
Germany had annexed Alsace-Lorraine in 1871 after the Franco-Prussian War. In total the treaty cost it about one seventh of its territory.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-28: Under which treaty did Hungary lose about two thirds of its former territory in 1920?
Trianon was one of the Paris peace treaties; afterwards millions of Hungarians lived in neighbouring states. Saint-Germain concerned Austria, Neuilly Bulgaria and Sèvres the Ottoman Empire.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-29: Which principle was at the heart of US President Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points of 1918?
The restoration of the monarchy in Russia
The division of Germany into occupation zones
Wilson also called for open diplomacy, freedom of the seas and a League of Nations. In the peace treaties, however, self-determination was applied unevenly.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-30: In which city was the League of Nations based?
The League first met in 1920; Germany was admitted in 1926 and left again under Hitler in 1933. Its Palais des Nations is used today by the United Nations.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-31: Which of these League of Nations mandates was administered by France?
France received the mandates for Syria and Lebanon, Britain those for Palestine, Transjordan and Iraq. The borders largely followed the secret Sykes-Picot Agreement of 1916.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-32: Why did the right-wing Kapp Putsch fail in March 1920?
Because of a general strike and the refusal of civil servants to cooperate
Because of a ruling by the Supreme Court
Because the army leadership immediately attacked the putschists
The army had refused to act against the putschists; the republic was saved by a general strike called by the trade unions and the SPD. After a few days Kapp and Lüttwitz gave up.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-33: Who was murdered by Freikorps soldiers together with Rosa Luxemburg in January 1919?
Luxemburg and Liebknecht had co-founded the KPD at the turn of 1918/19. Eisner, Erzberger and Rathenau also fell victim to political murders in the following years.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-34: In which city did Adolf Hitler attempt a putsch in November 1923?
The putschists' march was stopped by police at the Feldherrnhalle. While imprisoned in Landsberg, Hitler wrote "Mein Kampf".
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-35: How many marks did one US dollar cost at the peak of hyperinflation in November 1923?
Before the war a dollar had cost about 4.20 marks. Inflation wiped out the savings of the middle class and shook confidence in the republic.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-36: With which French foreign minister did Gustav Stresemann receive the Nobel Peace Prize in 1926?
Both were honoured for the policy of reconciliation that led to the Locarno Treaties in 1925 and Germany's admission to the League of Nations in 1926.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-37: Which article of the Weimar Constitution allowed the Reich President to issue emergency decrees without parliament?

From 1930 the presidential cabinets under Heinrich Brüning governed almost entirely by emergency decree, weakening parliament. Article 231, by contrast, was the war-guilt clause of the Treaty of Versailles.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-38: What made Albert Einstein world-famous overnight in 1919?
The Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity
The first artificial splitting of an atomic nucleus
The confirmation of his theory of relativity during a solar eclipse

During the solar eclipse of May 1919 British astronomers measured the bending of starlight by the sun that Einstein had predicted. He later received the Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-39: What did the image of the "New Woman" stand for in the 1920s?
Women who returned entirely to the home after the war
Working, self-confident women with bobbed hair and short skirts
Aristocratic ladies who carried on the court society of the Empire
Farm women who rebuilt agriculture after the war
Office workers, secretaries and shop assistants shaped big-city life in the Weimar years. Yet this new self-confidence coexisted with continuing disadvantages, for example in wages.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-40: Who wrote the anti-war novel "All Quiet on the Western Front"?
Published as a book in 1929, the novel describes the war from the perspective of a young soldier and became a worldwide success. The Nazis burned it in 1933.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-41: Who made the first non-stop solo flight across the Atlantic in 1927?
Lindbergh flew from New York to Paris in about 33 hours. Amelia Earhart repeated the feat in 1932 as the first woman.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-42: What did Alexander Fleming discover in 1928?
Fleming noticed that a mould killed bacteria. Penicillin was only produced as a drug in large quantities during the Second World War.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-43: Through which event did Benito Mussolini come to power in Italy in 1922?
An election victory with an absolute majority
A military coup by the army leadership
The Lateran Treaties with the Pope
Under pressure from the marching Fascists, King Victor Emmanuel III appointed Mussolini prime minister. In the following years he established the first fascist dictatorship.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-44: Which state was created in 1929 by the Lateran Treaties between Mussolini and the Pope?
The treaties ended the dispute between Italy and the papacy that had lasted since the loss of the Papal States in 1870. Catholicism also became Italy's state religion.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-45: How did Stalin have prominent former comrades of Lenin condemned during the Great Purge?
Through referendums in the Soviet republics
Before a League of Nations court
In public show trials with forced confessions
Through secret ballots at the party congress
In the Moscow trials of 1936 to 1938, Zinoviev, Kamenev and Bukharin among others were sentenced to death. Hundreds of thousands more were shot without trial.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-46: In which city did the Great Depression begin with a stock market crash in October 1929?
The collapse on Wall Street from "Black Thursday" onward dragged down banks and companies worldwide. Because American loans were withdrawn, the crisis hit Germany especially hard.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-47: What was the name of the reform programme with which US President Franklin D. Roosevelt fought the Great Depression?
The New Deal relied on public works, banking regulation and, with the Social Security Act of 1935, social insurance. The other terms denote programmes of later or earlier presidents.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-48: Which Chinese region did Japan occupy in 1931?
In 1932 Japan set up the puppet state of Manchukuo there, headed by the last emperor Puyi. When the League of Nations condemned this, Japan withdrew in 1933.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-49: Which politician rose to the leadership of the Chinese Communists during the Long March of 1934/35?
The Red Army's retreat covered some 12,000 kilometres to north-western China; only a fraction of those who set out arrived. The march became the founding myth of the Communist Party.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-50: Which African country did Fascist Italy invade in 1935?
The League of Nations imposed only half-hearted sanctions, and Emperor Haile Selassie had to go into exile. The war exposed the League's powerlessness against aggressors.
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-51: Which Basque town did the German Condor Legion destroy from the air in 1937 during the Spanish Civil War?
The attack on the civilian population caused horror around the world. Pablo Picasso responded the same year with his famous painting "Guernica".
q-erster-weltkrieg-zwischenkriegszeit-52: Who led the Nationalists to victory in the Spanish Civil War?
With German and Italian help, Franco defeated the Republic in 1939 and ruled Spain as dictator until his death in 1975.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-01#question: What is the name of the oldest known writing system in the world, developed by the Sumerians?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-01#explanation: Around 3200 BC the Sumerians pressed wedge-shaped signs into clay tablets; hence the name cuneiform, from the Latin for wedge.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-02#question: Which river was the lifeline of ancient Egypt?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-02#explanation: The annual Nile flood brought fertile silt and made Egypt a rich agricultural land.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-03#question: What is the Babylonian king Hammurabi best known for?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-03#choices.2: For the invention of the wheel
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-03#explanation: Around 1750 BC Hammurabi had some 280 legal provisions recorded on a stele, the Code of Hammurabi.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-04#question: Which pharaoh worshipped the sun disk Aten alone and founded the city of Akhetaten?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-04#explanation: Akhenaten banned the old cults of the gods and moved the capital to Akhetaten, near present-day Amarna.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-05#question: Between which powers was the oldest surviving peace treaty concluded after the Battle of Kadesh?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-05#explanation: Ramesses II and the Hittite king Hattusili III agreed on peace and mutual assistance about 15 years after the battle.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-06#question: Which sources provide the oldest evidence of Chinese writing?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-06#choices.1: Stone tablets of the Great Wall
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-06#choices.2: Bamboo books of the Zhou period
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-06#choices.3: Oracle bones of the Shang dynasty
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-06#explanation: The Shang kings scratched their questions to the ancestors into ox bones and turtle shells; these inscriptions are the oldest Chinese written records.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-07#question: Who is regarded as the first author in world history known by name?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-07#explanation: Enheduanna, daughter of Sargon of Akkad and high priestess in Ur, names herself as the author in her hymns.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-08#question: Which people developed an alphabet of 22 letters around 1050 BC that the Greeks later adopted?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-08#explanation: The Phoenicians of Tyre, Sidon and Byblos simplified writing to 22 consonant signs; the Greeks added vowels.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-09#question: What, among other things, is the Epic of Gilgamesh about?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-09#explanation: After the death of his friend Enkidu, Gilgamesh seeks out Utnapishtim, the hero of the flood, in order to gain eternal life, and fails.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-10#question: Which civilization built palaces such as Knossos on Crete?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-10#explanation: The Minoans, named after the legendary king Minos, created the first advanced civilization in Europe from around 2000 BC.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-11#question: What was remarkable about Fu Hao, the consort of the Shang king Wu Ding?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-11#choices.0: As a woman she led armies into battle
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-11#choices.2: She ruled as the first empress of China
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-11#choices.3: She built the first Great Wall
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-11#explanation: Oracle bones report that Fu Hao commanded campaigns with thousands of soldiers; her unplundered tomb was discovered at Anyang in 1976.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-12#question: Where was the kingdom of Kush, whose king Piye conquered Egypt around 730 BC?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-12#explanation: Kush, with its capitals at Napata and later Meroe, lay south of Egypt on the Nile; its kings formed the 25th Dynasty.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-13#question: In which city did cuneiform writing emerge around 3200 BC?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-13#explanation: In Uruk scribes first recorded taxes and stores with pictographs on clay tablets, from which the abstract wedge-shaped signs developed.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-14#question: With what and on what was cuneiform usually written?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-14#choices.1: With a reed stylus in damp clay
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-14#explanation: The signs were pressed into the clay as wedges; dried or fired tablets survived for millennia, and the script was used for over 3,000 years for many languages.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-15#question: According to tradition, which king united Upper and Lower Egypt around 3100 BC?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-15#explanation: Menes, probably the same ruler shown on the Narmer Palette, is also said to have founded the capital Memphis; this marked the beginning of pharaonic Egypt.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-16#question: Which script did the ancient Egyptians use for inscriptions on temple walls and tombs?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-16#explanation: This picture script arose around 3200 BC; its signs stand for sounds, syllables or whole words and were also written on papyrus.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-17#question: What did the Egyptian word from which the title pharaoh derives mean?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-17#explanation: It originally referred to the royal palace; only later did the word come to mean the king himself, who was regarded as the son of the sun god.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-18#question: What was the name of the divine world order of truth and justice that the pharaoh was meant to uphold?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-18#explanation: The pharaoh was seen as the guarantor of Maat against chaos; the goddess of the same name was depicted with a feather that was weighed against the heart at the judgement of the dead.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-19#question: According to current research, who built the Great Pyramid of Khufu?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-19#choices.0: Nubian prisoners of war held as slaves
